_about: The words of the launch video (assets/src/video.ts), scene by scene. Every figure is one the README or tested.md gives: {braced} names are filled in when the video is built, the sign-up's numbers from idea-counts.json through hundred.ts and the evidence's from the checks' own results in evals/. A *starred* phrase is drawn in the accent.

asks: How many of them are there?

person.name: Woman, 76. Cardiff, Wales.
rows: Retired, last worked more than 5 years ago
Owned outright, 20 years or more at this address
Finding it difficult to get by
Every day, on a smartphone and tablet; not very confident
person.head: Each has *150 facts,* and they fit together.

matched.head: As a group, they match official statistics
matched.if: If about *22 in 100* of them are retired and free on weekday mornings,
matched.so: about *22 in 100* real adults are too.

count.context: One choice on a sign-up page, counted for adults in the UK
count.choice: “You can only sign up in our app, on a smartphone.”
count.label: counted
count.note: Each square is 1 in 100 adults in the UK. Counted on 200,000 made-up adults that match official statistics.

groups.who: go online, but not on a smartphone

scan.model_what: An AI model that, given a question and its possible answers, says how likely each answer is.
scan.question: sees your sign-up page. What do they do next?
scan.one: It asks about *one fact at a time.*
scan.all: Then each of the 200,000 gets an answer built from *all their facts.*
scan.counted: So who leans in is *counted and broken down,* like any count.
scan.note: A sketch of how a scan works. No result is shown.

steps: Writes your idea a few ways
Finds which groups lean in to each
research.cost: Counts are free, on your computer. Scans are about 2 US cents a version, on your own key.
parts: Strong leads first, each sized and broken down
The cheapest real test that would tell the leading two apart

look.point: A way out of the twelve months: a year's contract with no way out is harder for *about 40 in every 100 adults in Cardiff,* who find money hard or are just getting by
look.label: counted
look.what: *A second look:* at most three points, or one line saying none.

meet.what: *A panel* puts faces to a count.
meet.sub: The group counted, and a few of its people drawn at random, each a card of their own facts.

context.head: Each runs in its own context, *only when you ask.*
context.sub: Until you ask, Claude works, and costs, exactly as it would without nxk.

checked.labels_head: Every figure says *where it came from.*
checked.from: From a count: *counted.* From a scan: *simulated.*
checked.head: Checked against published figures

rows.text: counts on nxk's made-up US adults came within 2 points of real adults in the Census Bureau's 2024 survey
differences between groups in 22 official surveys, put the right way round by the decision model
differences in who uses 32 existing products, put the right way round by a scan
